items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: You and I were at a dinner table with Bucky and Ruth.

ctx.x: How do you learn all the tunes that you need to know as a bass player? And you must have to tell your students something about that.

Well, it’s funny, sometimes there’s two schools of thought in jazz. Bucky Pizzarelli, when he was at William Paterson, boy, I mean I knew some that studied with him, he really got on kids’ cases. I think Bucky can do it and get away with it, he’s just so wonderful. He’d get on kids’ cases about learning tunes and having repertoire. I’m not sure if that’s always really the focus in schools. You know what I mean? I’m not sure about that. There was a set repertoire that I had to learn when I was back at the…
Did that education prepare you very well for the real world?

items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: That’s right. Bucky Pizzarelli and Ruth Pizzarelli, and Wallace Roney and many others.

ctx.x: There was a week, I believe near the end of March, where it seemed like every other day there was an obit.
That’s right. Bucky Pizzarelli and Ruth Pizzarelli, and Wallace Roney and many others.
And it just seemed like whoa, why is this hitting these older musicians with such regularity. And I remember thinking well Bucky was not in great health. We had almost lost him a couple of years ago.
